status_summary: On 2025-12-11 the President signed Congressional Review Act resolutions disapproving four Biden-era BLM plan decisions (Miles City, North Dakota, Central Yukon, Buffalo) and the Coastal Plain leasing record of decision (Public Laws 119-48 to 119-52). BLM began amending the 2024 Rock Springs plan on 2025-10-02 and on 2026-06-04 ended its Buffalo amendment process, leaving the 2015 plan as amended in 2019 in effect. Separately, BLM proposed on 2025-09-11 and finalized on 2026-05-12 (effective 2026-06-11) the rescission of its 2024 Conservation and Landscape Health Rule.

timeline.event: BLM proposed rescinding the 2024 Conservation and Landscape Health Rule.
BLM published a notice of intent to amend the Rock Springs Field Office resource management plan in Wyoming.
President signed joint resolutions disapproving the Miles City, North Dakota, Central Yukon and Buffalo plan decisions and the Coastal Plain leasing record of decision (Public Laws 119-48 to 119-52).
BLM published the final rescission of the Conservation and Landscape Health Rule, effective 2026-06-11.
BLM published termination of the Buffalo Field Office plan amendment process.

title: Review recent BLM land plans and drop conservation-first management decisions
uncertainties: The Mandate does not name the 2024 public lands rule in this passage, so that rescission is treated as part of the same policy direction, not as a literal match. Review of every plan from the prior four years is only partly documented, and the Rock Springs amendment had no later Federal Register notice in an API search. Public law numbers for H.J.Res. 104, 105, 106 and 131 come from GovInfo bill status; the Buffalo law number (119-51) comes from the 2026-06-04 notice.
